mirror neurons can be modulated by associative learning, that this modulation can be long-lasting, and that the modulation is stimulus specific.
mirror neurons are a genetically specified neural system that can be modified by learning and experience.
the human mirror neuron system, which is involved in imitation, action understanding, and language, is genetically specified, but its function is shaped by experience.

the neural basis of the human capacity to learn and use symbols.
how the brain represents and processes information about the world.
how we can use the brain as a tool for understanding how the mind works.

mirror neurons are part of the neural machinery for understanding actions and that this is the most plausible hypothesis to date.
the mirror neuron system is an innate, genetically determined neural circuit that has been adapted to support the learning of motor skills and social cognition.
we are not yet sure about what mirror neurons are for, and this is a very important question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mirror neuron system is not a unitary system, but is rather a collection of neural systems that share some properties.
mirror neurons are not the “missing link” between perception and action, nor are they the basis for the “theory of mind” or the basis for language.
the mirror neuron system is a system of neural circuits, which is genetically determined, and which has the ability to learn.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neural mechanisms that underlie imitation and other social behaviors are not as simple as previously thought, but that the basic neural organization of the mirror neuron system is consistent with a role in social cognition.
the mirror neuron system is not a unitary system, but rather a collection of functionally distinct sub-systems, each with its own evolutionary history.
